=== named types
tariff "t"
input a: Bool
input b: Int = 1
input c: Weight
---
tariff "t"
input a: Bool
input b: Int = 1
input c: Weight

=== generic list
tariff "t"
input breaks: List<Break>
input nested: List<List<Int>>
---
tariff "t"
input breaks: List<Break>
input nested: List<List<Int>>

=== rate types
tariff "t"
input a: Money/cwt
input b: Money/Weight
input c: Weight/Volume
input d: lb/ft3
---
tariff "t"
input a: Money/cwt
input b: Money/Weight
input c: Weight/Volume
input d: lb/ft3

=== optional types
tariff "t"
input a: Money?
input b: Money/mi?
input c: List<Stop>?
---
tariff "t"
input a: Money?
input b: Money/mi?
input c: List<Stop>?

=== record type in an input
tariff "t"
input a: { min: Weight, max: Weight? }
---
tariff "t"
input a: {min: Weight, max: Weight?}

=== record type with keyword field names
tariff "t"
input a: { in: Int, to: Int }
---
tariff "t"
input a: {in: Int, to: Int}

=== types in parameters and returns
library "l"
fn f(a: List<Break>, b: Money/cwt = $1/cwt) -> { weight: Weight, deficit: Bool } = { weight: 1 lb, deficit: false }
---
library "l"
fn f(a: List<Break>, b: Money/cwt = $1/[cwt]) -> {weight: Weight, deficit: Bool} = (record weight:1[lb] deficit:false)

=== type annotation on a let
tariff "t"
let a: Money/mi = $1/mi
let b: List<Text> = []
---
tariff "t"
let a: Money/mi = $1/[mi]
let b: List<Text> = (list)

=== temperature unit in a type
tariff "t"
input a: Money/°F
---
tariff "t"
input a: Money/°F

=== missing type
tariff "t"
input a:
---
tariff "t"
input a: ?
! syntax 19..19 Expected a type, like `Money`, `Weight` or `List<Stop>`

=== missing type argument
tariff "t"
input a: List<>
---
tariff "t"
input a: List
! syntax 24..25 Expected a type inside `<…>`

=== unclosed type argument
tariff "t"
input a: List<Int
---
tariff "t"
input a: List<Int>
! syntax 24..25 This `<` is missing its closing `>`

=== double optional
tariff "t"
input a: Int??
---
tariff "t"
input a: Int?
! syntax 23..25 A type is optional once; one `?` is enough

=== quotient without a denominator
tariff "t"
input a: Money/
---
tariff "t"
input a: Money/
! syntax 26..26 Expected a unit or a dimension after `/`, like `Money/cwt` or `Money/Weight`

=== empty record type
tariff "t"
input a: {}
---
tariff "t"
input a: {}
! syntax 20..22 A record type needs at least one field

=== input without a type
tariff "t"
input a = 5
---
tariff "t"
input a: ? = 5
! syntax 19..20 Expected `:` and the input's type after `a`
